title: Here's the Torcal, the first fully electric Bentley
gist: Bentley unveiled the Torcal, its first battery EV, built on Porsche-shared Volkswagen Group technology with 810–875 hp, a 113 kWh 800 V pack charging at up to 400 kW, and 375-mile WLTP range. It slots below the Bentayga in size and price and goes on sale in the US early next year.

insights.claim: The Torcal, Bentley's first battery EV, is smaller than the Bentayga and expected to slot beneath it (or its PHEV version) in pricing, with US pricing not yet revealed and US sales starting early next year.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: An entry-level position for Bentley's first EV tests ultra-luxury demand for electrification; watch pricing and order uptake.
insights.locator: A few weeks ago, Bentley gave Ars a ride

insights.claim: The Torcal shares underpinnings with Porsche within the Volkswagen Group, including the same curved OLED infotainment screen as the electric Cayenne, though with less power than the electric Cayenne.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Platform sharing spreads Volkswagen Group EV development costs across luxury brands, supporting margins on low-volume models.
insights.locator: Underneath the bodywork are some relatively familiar underpinnings

insights.claim: The standard Torcal produces 810 hp and 880 lb-ft for a 3.3-second 0–60 mph time and 155 mph top speed, while the Torcal S produces 875 hp and 995 lb-ft for 2.8 seconds to 60 mph and a 162 mph top speed.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Performance parity with ICE flagships is table stakes for luxury EV acceptance.
insights.locator: The more powerful Torcal S boasts 875 hp

insights.claim: The Torcal uses a 113 kWh net, 800 V battery pack with DC fast charging up to 400 kW, taking just under 20 minutes from 10–80 percent, and is rated at 375 miles WLTP with an EPA estimate expected to be at least 300 miles.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: 800 V architecture and 400 kW charging set the charging benchmark luxury EV competitors must match.
insights.locator: An official US EPA range estimate should be forthcoming

insights.claim: Bentley tuned the heavier Torcal's suspension, pedal calibration and steering response to feel familiar to existing customers, uses active ride suspension to combine Flying Spur comfort with GT-like dynamics, and can simulate the sound of a 6.75 L V8.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Legacy luxury brands are trying to retain ICE loyalists by replicating familiar driving character in EVs.
insights.quote: you’ve got the ride comfort and compliance from a Flying Spur, but in a dynamic environment, we’ve got a vehicle that’s as dynamic and capable as a GT,
insights.locator: Although it’s a much heavier car

insights.claim: The Torcal interior offers merino wool fabric and a veneer made from up to 1,000 walnut offcuts, but replaces traditional metal 'organ stopper' vent controls with touchscreen-aimed vents, which the author considers regrettable.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Cost- and platform-driven touchscreen controls can dilute luxury differentiation, a potential customer friction point.
insights.locator: We can also see the full interior finally
